Exactly-once means each message is processed one time and one time only, so a duplicate never lands downstream. At-least-once means every message is processed at least once, but a retry after a failure can deliver the same message twice, so the consumer has to be built to handle repeats.

In practice, at-least-once is the honest default for most streaming systems, because you can always retry and you rarely lose data. True exactly-once is harder, since it usually means transactions or idempotent writes so a redelivery does not change the result.
